comparison: Perfect agreement on C5-C6 (total brain volume sex differences). Both evaluations find the evidence solid and well-supported by appropriate statistical analyses with adequate sample sizes.

Perfect agreement on C7-C10 (tissue-specific volume findings). Both evaluations affirm the evidence is solid and methods are appropriate, though OpenEval notes the marginal significance (p=0.045) of mouse white matter finding warrants caution.
Perfect agreement on C11-C18 (regional sex differences with effect sizes). Both evaluations confirm the evidence is solid with appropriate statistical methods including FDR correction.

Strong agreement on C19-C22 (regional patterns). Both evaluations support these claims, with peer review also grouping C23-C25 (conservation/divergence patterns) together, while OpenEval evaluates these separately in R5.

Both address C23-C25 (patterns of conservation and divergence). OpenEval notes these involve some inference about biological significance, while peer review groups them with C19-C22 and affirms the study successfully identifies conserved vs. non-conserved aspects.

Strong agreement on C26-C29 (variance differences). Both evaluations support these claims based on Levene's test results. Peer review also includes C55-C57 (heterogametic theory challenge) in the same evaluation, while OpenEval addresses these separately in R14.

Both address C55-C57 (variance patterns and heterogametic theory). OpenEval notes this represents one piece of evidence rather than definitive refutation, while peer review groups these with C26-C29 and affirms the evidence is solid.

Both address C30-C31 (correlation between species). OpenEval notes modest but significant overall correlation with loss of significance in stratified analyses. Peer review groups these with C32-C41 and describes 'modest convergence' as a key finding.

Strong overlap on C32-C40 (conserved sex differences). Both evaluations support these claims with FDR-corrected analyses. Peer review also includes C30-C31 and C41, while OpenEval addresses C41 separately in R9.

Both address C41 (divergent amygdala findings). OpenEval notes significant effects in opposite directions between species. Peer review groups this with the broader correlation analysis (C30-C40) as part of the modest convergence finding.

Strong agreement on C42-C45 (anatomical-transcriptional correlations). Both evaluations support the methodological approach. OpenEval notes the marginally non-significant overall correlation (p=0.08) but strong cortical significance. Peer review also includes C46-C47, C54, and C69.

Both address C46-C47 (regional differentiation in correlations). OpenEval notes appropriate synthesis with some interpretive inference. Peer review groups these with the broader transcriptional analysis (C42-C45, C54, C69) and affirms solid evidence.

Strong agreement on C48-C51 (hormone pathway gene analyses). Both evaluations support the sensitivity analyses. OpenEval notes most correlations don't reach significance and suggest hypotheses rather than definitive conclusions. Peer review also includes C71-C73.

Both address C71-C73 (differential hormone roles). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting C73's interpretation is speculative based on gene expression patterns rather than direct hormone measurements. Peer review groups with C48-C51 but notes the study 'do not provide any evidence as to the mechanisms.'

Both address C52-C53 (major findings synthesis). OpenEval supports these as appropriate summary of evidence for divergence and conservation. Peer review groups with C74, C92-C93 and explicitly acknowledges the study demonstrates which aspects are conserved across species.

Both address C92-C93 (correlation analysis synthesis). OpenEval supports these as well-supported by stratified analyses showing stronger cortical correlations. Peer review groups with C52-C53 and C74 as part of the main conclusion about cross-species relevance.

Both address C58-C61 (mechanistic context from literature). OpenEval supports these as properly attributed literature-based claims. Peer review groups with extensive mechanistic discussion (C62-C91) but rates as UNCERTAIN, noting 'these data do not provide any evidence as to the mechanisms.'

Both address C62-C65 (hormone sensitivity speculation). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting speculative language and inferential mechanistic interpretations. Peer review groups with broader mechanistic discussion and explicitly identifies lack of mechanistic evidence as a limitation.

Both address C66-C70 (cellular mechanisms and transcriptional findings). OpenEval supports these as well-grounded in cited evidence though speculative. Peer review groups with extensive mechanistic discussion (C58-C91) and rates as UNCERTAIN due to lack of direct mechanistic evidence.

Both address C74-C79 (developmental timing and perinatal hormones). OpenEval supports C74-C77 with citations but notes C78-C79 represent hypothesis rather than demonstrated causation. Peer review groups with broader mechanistic discussion and identifies lack of evidence about when differences arise as a limitation.

Both address C80-C83 (species differences in hormone mechanisms). OpenEval supports these as appropriately citing organoid and mechanistic studies. Peer review groups with broader mechanistic discussion (C58-C91) and rates as UNCERTAIN due to lack of direct mechanistic evidence from current study.

Both address C84-C88 (sex chromosome effects). OpenEval supports these as appropriately citing aneuploidy studies and comparative genomics. Peer review groups with broader mechanistic discussion (C58-C91) and rates as UNCERTAIN, noting lack of mechanistic evidence.

Both address C89-C91 (conceptual caveats). OpenEval supports these as important caveats distinguishing sex from gender and cautioning against functional interpretations. Peer review groups with mechanistic discussion and notes lack of evidence about behavioral impact as a limitation.

Both address C94-C99 (neuropsychiatric and cognitive sex differences background). OpenEval supports these as well-supported motivational context from literature. Peer review groups with broader background claims (C1-C4, C100-C116) and affirms the study rationale.

Both address C100-C104 (prior human neuroimaging literature). OpenEval supports these as appropriately characterizing heterogeneity and reproducible findings. Peer review groups with broader background and affirms the study establishes appropriate context.

Strong agreement on C105-C114 (rodent literature review). Both evaluations support these as appropriately reviewing prior work and establishing rationale. Peer review groups with broader background claims and affirms practical implications for neuroscience.

Both address C115-C116 (study rationale and impact). OpenEval supports these as well-justified logical inferences. Peer review groups with broader background and explicitly affirms the goal 'has practical implications for multiple fields in neuroscience.'

Both address C117-C118 (sample descriptions). OpenEval supports these as accurate with adequate sample sizes. Peer review rates as UNCERTAIN, explicitly noting as a limitation 'the focus on a specific age range in mice and humans (which may not be congruent).'
